# HyperFrames 0.8.145 integration notes

## CLI forwarding

- The CLI rejects extra positional arguments and unknown flags. Voyager already
  runs inside the project directory: pass `render --format webm --output out/video.webm`, not
  an entry file, composition ID and output as positional arguments. Use
  `--composition` for another composition file.
- `snapshot --at 1 --no-end --describe false` captures a still. HyperFrames has
  no `still` or `export-html` command.
- `timeline` inspects tracks and has editing subcommands; `history` inspects and
  restores recorded changes. `clean` can remove global caches
  and caches in other recorded projects, even with a project directory argument;
  use it only for an explicit cleanup request. `open` hands off to upstream Studio;
  use the live preview for work inside Voyager.

## Installed documentation

- `gsap.md`'s “Supported Properties” is not an exhaustive list. `filter`,
  `clipPath`, `width` and `height` tween; lint rejects layout motion such as
  `left`, `top`, `margin`, `fontSize` and `letterSpacing`. Tweening
  `letterSpacing` fails lint as `gsap_non_transform_motion`; animate per-glyph
  spans' `x` instead.
- For raw media preparation, see
  [bundled FFmpeg encoders](../../make-social-loop/references/delivery.md#bundled-ffmpeg-encoders)
  (`libx264`/`libx265` are absent; probe the platform encoder first).
- Rendering quality names are `draft`, `looks` (default) and `delivery`.

## Sub-compositions

- Keep a template sub-composition's styles, markup and scripts inside its
  `<template>`. Full-document and bare-fragment sub-compositions are also
  supported. Do not wrap the top-level composition in a template.
- Give each `data-composition-src` host a `data-composition-id` even though the
  upstream example omits it. Match the host, inner root and timeline IDs.
- Use `fromTo` instead of `from`: re-seeking a sub-composition can make `from`
  read the wrong end state.

## Media and timing

- Timed audio/video needs an `id`. Time the video or its wrapper, not both.
  Omit media `crossorigin`; it can make preview blank while rendering works.
- Missing or unready media can still be skipped in the default best-effort mode;
  use `render --no-best-effort` to fail instead.
- Composition scripts start after web fonts load. Keep fonts local. GSAP `set` steps and tween starts
  now render on their landing frame; repeated `fromTo` baselines may need
  `immediateRender: false` so a later tween does not overwrite an earlier pose.
- Root duration and dimensions must be in static HTML; changing them in a script
  is ignored.
- Relative starts require spaces: `intro - 0.5`, not `intro-0.5`. Missing targets,
  typos and cycles silently resolve to zero.
- Visibility windows exclude their end time. Land a final pose before the end;
  clamp video slots to the remaining source duration to avoid frozen last frames.

## Crossfades and checks

- Paint an opaque background to avoid white showing through crossfades. Alpha
  exports now preserve the composition root's authored background; remove it
  when the output should be transparent.
- Rendering does not stop on lint errors unless `--strict` is passed.
- `sweep_static` reports identical sampled geometry. Inspect whether the timeline
  seeks or its reveal finished early; do not add motion just to silence a finding.
- Keep animation on
  the seekable timeline; mark an intentionally static host `data-no-timeline`.

# Rights and delivery

For asset rights, credits, subtitles and delivery checks.

## Core

- Deliver a `CREDITS` file naming every third-party asset (samples, music, fonts, images, the voice engine) with its source and licence; credit on screen where a licence requires it; tell the user `CREDITS` lists the licences and the material is their responsibility.
- When anything is spoken, offer an `.srt` in one line.
- `voyager media review FILE` measures loudness but flags only a true peak above 0 dBTP (clipping): check `audio.integratedLUFS` near −14 and `audio.truePeakDBTP` at or below −1 yourself. It also checks black frames and duration. Re-level with two-pass `loudnorm` (`TP=-1`, `linear=true`, the first pass's measured values) and review again before presenting.
- To judge continuous motion, sync or how a clip sounds, use a video-understanding model with `voyager models run`; load `choose-media-model/references/understanding.md` for the paid upload route.

# Reading time

Every text on screen must stay fully inside the frame, unchanged, for at least
max(1.5, CJK characters ÷ 4.5 + other characters ÷ 15 + 1.5) seconds.
`voyager hyperframes readcheck ./<piece>/motion` seeks the composition every 0.05 s with the
renderer's own seek, so clip windows (`data-start`/`data-duration`) count.

- A text change under the same element starts a new piece, so a typewriter or an
  animated counter (0 → 100) fails once per change. Give that element `data-full-text="…"` with the finished text; it is
  then judged as a whole from its first visible frame.
- Caption bands are timed by their cues, not here: mark the container
  `data-layout-allow-caption-zone` (the flag `check` already uses) and it is skipped,
  as is `data-layout-ignore`.
- `--selector "#card h2"` checks only those elements, each as one text. `--min`,
  `--pad`, `--latin-cps`, `--cjk-cps` and `--step` change the rule; deliver with the
  defaults.

---
name: edit-in-hyperframes
description: "."
applications:
  - id: hyperframes
    role: primary
voyager:
  schemaVersion: 1
  design: optional
  craft: [rights-and-delivery]
---

Create one project per piece inside the active workspace, named for the piece.
Never add a piece to another piece's project; reuse a project only to revise its piece.

```sh
voyager hyperframes setup ./<piece>/motion --json
voyager hyperframes run ./<piece>/motion -- <HyperFrames CLI arguments>
```

Setup installs HyperFrames 0.8.145 and pinned Chrome and returns the installed docs
path. Initial setup downloads Chrome Headless Shell and can take several minutes;
give the setup command a long shell timeout. For an existing project, setup refuses an incompatible manifest and lists the
required pins: explicitly pin every listed dependency in `package.json`, including
GSAP. No package-manager lockfile is required before setup: setup validates the
manifest, then runs npm install.
Edit `index.html`; keep the starter's local GSAP. HyperFrames loads nothing outside the
project folder: copy brand-kit fonts and logos into its `assets/` and reference them
relatively (a `../brand/...` font gives "Fonts: 0 loaded, 2 failed" in `snapshot`). If unfamiliar with HyperFrames,
read `compositions.md` and `gsap.md` there. For upstream documentation corrections and silent
render failures, see [authoring gotchas](references/authoring-gotchas.md).

Animate through paused GSAP timelines registered on `window.__timelines`, not
timers or wall-clock animation.
Register each timeline after its elements and any async setup are ready.

For local previews, pass `--describe false` to `snapshot` and `--skip-vision` to
`capture`; otherwise configured API credentials can cause image uploads for AI
analysis. Use local authoring commands rather than upstream account, cloud,
publishing or installation commands.

Run `lint --json` and resolve errors before `check --json`; lint errors skip browser
checks.
When parsing JSON, read stdout only; do not merge stderr with `2>&1`.
Progress notices and live tool output go to stderr.
Then `voyager hyperframes readcheck ./<piece>/motion` checks that every text stays in
frame long enough to read; the rule is in [reading time](references/verification.md).
On Windows/Linux, render `--format webm`, then convert with
`voyager media assemble`; direct MP4 rendering here requires macOS.
`render --format mov` is ProRes 4444 with alpha: with no page background it is a transparent
overlay for an editor's upper video track.

For continuous motion, sync or how a clip sounds, use [watch and listen](../choose-media-model/references/understanding.md) (paid upload).
